route: exact re-run of data/mturk_ddm.R over the raw OSF deposit (core model s3), corroborated by paper Table 5 per-numerosity accuracy (route 1)
evidence: Re-ran data/mturk_ddm.R's Experiment-2 task-2 block over the raw OSF file (osf.io/za9y8, Experiment2.data, md5-stable public deposit) and compared per-item n and mean resp against irw_fetch: all 12/12 items identical -- 10 1 n=10622 mean=0.8790246658 vs 10622/0.8790246658; 20 1 n=10614 mean=0.6186169210 vs 10614/0.6186169210; 40 2 n=10616 mean=0.9109834213 vs 10616/0.9109834213; largest deviation over all 12 items 0.0e+00, all n differences 0. That reproduces the item code (paste(column_7_value, column_8_value)) and the resp direction (1 = correct) exactly, so it pins every one of the 12 codes including the area flag digit. Corroborated independently by the paper's Table 5 Pr('large') per numerosity, converted to accuracy: 10 0.898/0.884, 15 0.843/0.826, 20 0.641/0.630, 30 0.850/0.844, 35 0.904/0.896, 40 0.917/0.909 (paper/live), largest gap 0.017, consistent with the paper reporting 92 screened subjects while IRW pools all 166. What this does NOT establish: anything about item_text, which is blank by design (dot-array stimuli, no wording); and the area-flag digit is pinned ONLY by the exact re-run, since the paper states the area variable had almost no effect and the live 'N 1' vs 'N 2' means differ by at most 0.022, so no statistical route could separate the two area conditions.

route: source answer-key reproduction (Step 5b route 9 variant: re-score deposit raw responses with the shipped key and match the authors' own scoring, cell for cell)
evidence: Re-scored the deposit's own raw data against the shipped keys: for each item, participant's raw 20-bit element-selection string (X_MRnn_ww in tte_data.csv) == shipped correct_response, compared to the authors' scored Y_MRnn_ww. Exact agreement 24737/24737 (per item 1240/1240, 1239/1239, ... 1198/1198 for MR15), i.e. 100.00% for all 20 items. The keys are item-specific: the best-agreeing OTHER item's key falls to 0.2589 (MR01), 0.4746 (MR03), 0.5306 (MR04) ... max 0.7927, so 18 of 20 items are uniquely identified by their own key. DOES NOT ESTABLISH: (a) nothing about item wording -- item_text is blank by design (figural OMIB stimuli, images only), so no item-text mapping exists to test; (b) MR11 and MR12 share an identical published solution code '01000000000000000000' and agree with each other's key at 1.0000, so this route cannot distinguish that one pair -- they are separated only by the codebook's number-preserving column names, and a swap between them would change nothing shipped; (c) it says nothing about the option_text 'Incorrect'/'Correct' labels, which are the codebook's documented 0/1 scoring direction, not a verified mapping.
